features: THE CASH BOOK IS NO LONGER A PLACEHOLDER — The menu entry had been there for months with an "In development" badge and a link that led nowhere. Behind it there is now the cash register required by article 1130, paragraph 1, no. 7 of the Italian Civil Code: money in and money out, in chronological order, with a running balance. It is the actual legal obligation — the one the General Ledger, which holds every double-entry record including those that move no money at all, does not replace.

TWO DATES ON EVERY LINE, AS THE LAW REQUIRES — The register is ordered by the date the movement actually happened, and shows next to it the date it was recorded. When more than thirty days separate the two, the line says so: that is the deadline the law sets for recording, and proving it takes two dates, not one.

ONLY MONEY THAT ACTUALLY MOVES — An invoice recorded but not yet paid does not enter the register; neither does a transfer into the reserve fund, because that money stays in the same bank account. A withdrawal from the bank to petty cash, on the other hand, produces two lines — and that is correct: it is exactly why this register does not match the bank statement.

THE COUNTERPARTY IS RECONSTRUCTED, NOT LEFT BLANK — Who paid, or who was paid, is not stored in a single place: for a collection it is the unit owner, for a payment the supplier, for a withholding-tax payment the Revenue Agency, for an internal transfer the other cash account. The page looks for them in that order and shows the first one it finds.

THE BALANCE OF A SINGLE CASH ACCOUNT, BY OPENING THE ROW — The "Balance" column is the combined total across every real cash account, because the legal register is a single document. With two real accounts, though, that number alone does not say which one moved: the row detail shows the account involved and its balance right after that movement.

THE REGISTER CAN BE PRINTED — Same filters as the page: if you narrowed the period or searched a description, the printout contains only that and says so in a banner, with the total marked "partial". The General Ledger, which previously referred to this register in words only, now links to it for real — both on screen and in print.

EVERY MOVEMENT HAS ITS OWN NUMBER — The sources describing this register list the operation number among the minimum required data, before the date itself: it lets you cite a movement without describing it — «operation no. 47» instead of «that transfer back in May». Numbering is chronological across the financial year and does not change when you filter.

FILTERING A PERIOD NO LONGER CHANGES THE BALANCE — Looking at June alone, the «Balance» column still says how much was actually in the account on those days, not the net of the month: that is exactly why the law wants this register — to give «a continuous and direct check, in real time, of the accounts and of the money available to the building». The totals at the top are instead labelled as partial, because those do refer only to the movements shown. The same distinction holds in the per-account breakdown: each account's money in and out is as partial as the totals, its balance is not.

THE PRINTOUT HAS A LOOK OF ITS OWN — It is the first print in the system with its own typefaces, Inter for text and Fraunces for headings and amounts, instead of the generic default: the building's letterhead, small-caps column headings, aligned figures, double-ruled totals. It closes with a note explaining how the register is built, including reversed operations, which stay printed and marked because the civil code requires accounting records to remain legible even where they have been corrected (art. 2219).

THE TWO LEDGER PAGES NOW BEHAVE THE SAME — In both the Cash Book and the General Ledger, the link to an entry's detail now lives inside the panel that opens when you click a row, and the trailing icon column is gone from both: it was a second route to the same place, and in the General Ledger that panel offered no way through to the detail at all.

FIX — THE REVERSAL OF A WITHHOLDING-TAX PAYMENT WAS NOT LINKED TO THE ORIGINAL — It was the only reversal in the system that did not record the link back to the original entry, against the rule applied everywhere else in the product: a reversal never deletes, it writes an equal and opposite entry linked to the original. Anyone tracing back from the reversal to the payment no longer found it.

FIX — THE REGISTER'S PRINT CEILING NOW DERIVES FROM THE INSTALLATION'S MEMORY — Like the General Ledger's, instead of being a fixed number: an invented value higher than the already-measured threshold would have brought back silent mid-print failures on low-memory installations.

THE PRINTOUT NO LONGER REPORTS YOUR OWN DELAYS — On screen the register flags movements recorded later than the thirty days of art. 1130 § 1 no. 7 of the Civil Code, because that is the view you use to put things right. In print it does not: the sheet you take to the meeting carries only the date of the movement, the only one the law asks for. «Print» is now a two-item menu: «Print for the meeting» and «Control copy», which adds the recording dates and flags the delays — and says so at the top of the sheet, so the two versions cannot be mistaken for one another once printed.

THIS REGISTER IS ONE OF THE THREE DOCUMENTS OF THE ANNUAL STATEMENT, NOT THE WHOLE OF IT — Italian law (art. 1130-bis of the Civil Code) composes the annual statement of a cash register (this release's), a financial summary and an explanatory note. If you wrote to us over the summer asking for the full annual statement, this is the first half, delivered; the second half will come in a dedicated release, because it needs a piece of the accounting engine that is still missing — the year's result written at closing, not only computed on screen — and there is no point promising a statement that does not yet balance on its own.

FIX — REVERSING A COLLECTION NOW CARRIES THE REVERSAL DATE — It was the only one of the five reversals in the accounting module to take the date of the original collection instead of the day it was made. In the cash register, sorted by effective date, the reversal slotted in right after the collection and every running balance between the two dates said the money was not there — while it was, and only left on reversal. It now behaves like the other four: the collection on its date, the reversal on its own.

FIX — NO PAYMENTS OUT OF A FUND, NOT EVEN AS A DIRECT SETTLEMENT OR AN F24 — Supplier payments and collections already rejected a fund account (a fund is a partition of the current account: the money is released first with a transfer to the bank); direct settlements and F24 payments did not, and a payment made from a fund vanished from the cash register. They are now rejected like the others, and F24 payments only accept accounts of the right building.

TWO LIMITS STATED ON THE SHEET — The register's balance is net of the money set aside in funds, which is why it does not match the bank statement: it differs by what is tied up. And the running balance starts from zero at the beginning of the year: the carry-over from the previous year will come with the annual statement, in its dedicated release. Both are written in the «How to read this register» note and in the page's cards: whoever compares the sheet with the bank must learn it from the sheet.
